title: The Hidden Loss Penalty of On-Load Tap-Changer Voltage Regulation in Photovoltaic-Rich Four-Wire Low-Voltage Distribution Networks
content: On-load tap changers at medium- and low-voltage distribution substations are widely recommended to mitigate overvoltages in photovoltaic-rich low-voltage networks. This paper shows that this compliance comes with a systematic energy cost. Thus, a smart-meter-driven, four-wire planning tool with an explicit neutral, individual service cables, and an on-load tap changer with a representative reference pole was applied to a real Romanian network on its critical day in the summer season to demonstrate this aspect. Validated against professional software, DIgSILENT PowerFactory, (mean absolute voltage error 0.32 V, losses within 1.1%), the tool shows that the on-load tap changer removes all samples above 253 V but raises conductor losses by 17.7–18.3% for any reinforcement level. A calibrated ZIP load model confirms that the penalty persists (+15.6–17.9%) for conservation-voltage-reduction factors between 0 and 2, because 77% of the daily losses occur while the network exports and inverter currents dominate. Only the combination of 120 mm² phase conductors and an on-load tap changer is compliant and 17.4% less lossy than the current state, although the 70 mm² neutral then carries 31% of the losses. With an on-load tap changer, extended feeders host 30% instead of 20–21% prosumers, but the 250 kVA transformer reaches 96–101% loading, which becomes the binding limit for new connections.
